claims.text: Hypovolemic shock: fluid resuscitation w 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid over 3 h;
claims.quote: Typically, initial management of hypovolemic or distributive shock (including septic shock) is with fluid resuscitation: 30 mL/kg of balanced crystalloid solution, infused over 3 hours

claims.text: continued unless clinical parameters return to normal.
claims.quote: Unless clinical parameters return to normal, the infusion of fluid is typically continued.

claims.text: Hemorrhagic shock: surgical control of bleeding comes first; volume replacement accompanies it.
claims.quote: In hemorrhagic shock, surgical control of bleeding is the first priority. Volume replacement accompanies rather than precedes surgical measures to restore hemostasis.
claims.locator: Management of Shock › Management of hemorrhagic shock

claims.text: Massive transfusion: RBCs, FFP and platelets as soon as possible, in a 1:1:1 ratio;
claims.quote: Blood products--red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma, and platelets--are given as soon as possible and in a ratio of 1:1:1 in patients requiring massive transfusion.
claims.locator: Management of Shock › Management of hemorrhagic shock

claims.quote: Balanced crystalloid solutions are also used for resuscitation, as needed.
claims.locator: Management of Shock › Management of hemorrhagic shock

claims.text: Until hemorrhage control: restricted IV fluid volume (goal SBP 80 to 90 mm Hg or MAP 55 to 60; permissive hypotension) in most pts;
claims.quote: A restricted volume of IV fluid infusion (maintaining a goal systolic blood pressure of 80 to 90 mm Hg or MAP of 55 to 60 mm Hg; called hypotensive resuscitation or permissive hypotension) is recommended in most patients with hemorrhage shock until definitive hemorrhage control is achieved
claims.locator: Management of Shock › Management of hemorrhagic shock

claims.quote: however maintaining hypotension is contraindicated in patients with traumatic brain injury
claims.locator: Management of Shock › Management of hemorrhagic shock
